# Re-review rulings — 2026-10-27 (delegated: the user said "just use best judgment")

Marker for every edit that applies one of these: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling Rn)*.
In-text record where a decision is stated: "Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling Rn (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): ..."
These rulings never reverse a prior user ruling; they settle consequences the user's rulings left ambiguous or unimplementable.

## General rules (G)
- G1 Owner wins: where two GDDs disagree on a value, field, unit or contract, the registry `source:` GDD wins and the other conforms. If the thing is unregistered, the PUBLISHER of the field/signal/value wins and the consumer conforms.
- G2 Specialist disagreements: follow the creative-director's stated resolution in that GDD's disagreements list. Where the CD said "the user should choose", take the CD's stated lean.
- G3 Carried-over blockers (flagged "still not fixed"/"carried over"): previous edits did not land. After each edit, Grep for the old wording and confirm it is gone everywhere in the GDD (body, examples, ACs, tuning tables, OQs).
- G4 ACs that contradict the GDD's own formulas: recompute from the formula at registry defaults; never weaken a formula to match an AC.
- G5 Division/overflow at boundaries: guard explicitly (e.g. avail == 0 -> share 0, everything unserved); state the guard in the formula and add a boundary AC.

## Cross-cutting rulings (R)
- R1 Restore epoch (consequence of X8/D16). Save/Load OWNS `restore_epoch` as a persisted integer in the save slot header (u32, starts 0). On every restore (death restart or load), Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (atomic header-only write) BEFORE the first RUNNING tick, so reloading the same autosave twice, in-process or after a fresh process start, gives a new epoch each time. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as (T, world_seed, restore_epoch) — sim-visible, pure. The KERNEL (command-simulation-layer.md) owns the one derivation for threat draws, counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE x restore_epoch, and owns RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE (value 1048576 unchanged; registry_request: move its source from attention-system.md to command-simulation-layer.md, with attention, horror and save-load in referenced_by). The stream name hash stays cached and unchanged. Attention and Horror call the kernel derivation; neither defines its own. Graph physical failures and persisted counters never read the epoch. Determinism (G3/G4) is defined given (save bytes, restore_epoch): the same pair replays identically; tests pin the epoch. Required ACs: (i) two successive restores of the same save yield epochs e and e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) a fresh-process reload of the same slot also advances the epoch; (iii) same (save, epoch) pair -> identical draws. Save/Load's 'none of it able to alter the sim' is amended to exempt restore_epoch.
- R2 seq (kernel CR-4). The kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source); callers never choose it; `submit()` stays void (fire-and-forget). A caller may attach an opaque `correlation` field (int) that the kernel echoes unchanged in the result/rejection event. Player Controller keys pre-play tokens by `correlation`. Update the kernel seq ACs (L883, L892, L902-904) and PC-7 together.
- R3 Completion sentinel (kernel CR-19b). Every owner callable receives `ctx`; results flow through ctx, never the return value: validate reports via ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason); snapshot via ctx.put(payload); apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx). Every callable's only return is `return ctx.complete()` (a typed token). No `-> void` owner callables.
- R4 Mouse aim. The Player Controller's form is canonical: cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp - picture_centre) / k_eff, where f_q is the quantized camera position actually used for the frame. The Pipeline PUBLISHES f_q. Aim direction = cursor_aim_world - AIM_ORIGIN, with AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos) + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y) (ruling D10); remove the chest-based subtraction from the Pipeline's D.14b/D.7. Cursor units: the fixer must VERIFY the unit of the cursor source (e.g. Viewport.get_mouse_position() under the Pipeline's canvas_items stretch wiring (ii)) against docs/engine-reference/godot/ and the Pipeline's own wiring text, then make the label, the variable table and the divisor agree in both GDDs; if the reference cannot settle it, mark the unit claim [UNV] and add an in-engine verification AC.
- R5 Carry tell (consequence of X3). Owners: Attention owns the intake numbers and the ONE integrator (Attention's walk-in convention and tick accounting are canonical; Boarding quotes them); Boarding owns the live-choice acceptance (AC-BS-123) and its K definitions, stated with Attention's integrator; Derelict owns the route length (21-28 tiles, X3). Scope: the burden applies only to SALVAGE carry — an item carried that was picked up inside a non-home locus (derelict) — moving or standing, until dropped/installed/thrown; never to carrying at home or of the player's own kit. Pace-robustness, scoped to that salvage carry only: (a) while a salvage carry is held, attention decay is suspended (freezing with cargo is priced, per X3); (b) dropping and re-taking the same item grants no fresh TELL_REARM immunity (the rearm timer keys on the item, not the pickup). Attention may re-derive weights/theta within these scoped rules, but must NOT invent weights to force K3-K5 green: all values stay PLACEHOLDER, and if the live-choice margin cannot be shown on paper with honest numbers, AC-BS-123(d) is re-written as a spike gate (owner, the boarding spike, its pass line), which is the expected outcome.
- R6 Pod statuses (consequence of user ruling D60 "statuses run in the pod"). Suit's reading stands: the reserve drains, the cell drains while lit, source RESERVE. Web Map conforms: delete WM-17b's HOLD reading and close ASK-S2. Pillar-2 mitigation: the valve click plays only on the source TRANSITION edge (once when breath_src becomes RESERVE), never per run. Recompute every pod-leg figure from the registry's own leg formula at registry defaults (ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS default 45, not 180; the registry's formulas use 945 ticks per leg — verify in the registry before using) and state run counts with an explicit floor and a carried remainder so every "exactly N" oracle is an integer.
- R7 PD1 static spill bound (user ruling D31: 'static authored spill <= 24 px'). The bound stays 24 px — it is the user's number. The home ship's spine_corridor (computed 26 px) must be brought within it by Derelict Authoring (light placement, fixture position or corridor dressing — the least invasive change; show the recomputed s <= 24). Lighting's AC-LO-69 stays per-push BLOCKING.

## G6 Cross-GDD edits are now allowed
A blocker that needs a sibling GDD to change is fixed IN the sibling. Owner wins (G1): the registry `source:` GDD, else the publisher of the field/signal, keeps its value; the other conforms. Each file has exactly one writer per pass; requests to another file go to that file's writer.
Classify every blocker first: **CONFLICT** (the same thing has two values/contracts in two GDDs) -> the owner's value stands and the other GDD conforms; **GAP** (the owner lacks a surface, exemption, field or signal that a consumer's user-ruled or delegated-ruled behaviour requires, e.g. Interaction's act_gate exempt list lacking self-patch, HUD lacking a give_up surface) -> the OWNER ADDS it, and the consumer's requirement is the spec. Never "fix" a gap by removing the consumer's ruled behaviour.
Precedence: where R1 text conflicts with R13/R14, R13/R14 win; re-mark such text "delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14".

## R12 Reference machines and build (closes X14; supersedes R11)
- **RM-DESKTOP (minimum-spec desktop):** Windows 10/11 64-bit; 6-core/6-thread CPU of the Intel Core i5-9400F / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 class; 8 GB RAM; GPU of the NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB / AMD Radeon RX 570 4 GB class (Vulkan 1.2+); SATA SSD; 1920x1080 at 60 Hz. P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 16.6 ms.
- **RM-DECK (handheld):** Steam Deck LCD (2022), SteamOS stable, 1280x800 at 60 Hz panel, 30 fps target. P99 CPU frame-time ceiling 33.3 ms.
- **Build type for every wall-clock figure:** a release export (Godot 4.7.2 release export template, not the editor and not a debug template), renderer `forward_plus` (project.godot), vsync on, the pipeline's warm-up of 120 frames, with the startup read-back (renderer, driver) recorded with each result.
- **P99 headroom:** pass needs P99 <= 90 % of the ceiling (headroom >= 1.7 ms desktop, >= 3.3 ms Deck).
- The developer's machine is not a reference machine; figures from it are indicative only.
- Recorded in `project.yaml` as `qa.min_spec` (done by the orchestrator). In GDDs: replace "X14 open / not named / [blocked: reference hardware]" with the named machines; performance ACs become gated on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK at the spike (still measured at the spike, so a value not yet measured is "pending spike", not "blocked").

## R13 OQ-50: Continue of a Save & Quit keeps the epoch (amends R1)
User ruling D16 ("not steerable by quit") outranks delegated R1. A **death-stub restore** advances `restore_epoch` (durably, R14). A **Continue** that restores a `QUIT` generation which is the newest non-demoted verified generation **carries the epoch unchanged** (no epoch write). A Continue of any other generation (after a kill, crash or fallback) advances it. ACs: (i) death restore -> e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) Save & Quit, Continue -> same epoch, identical draws; (iii) kill, Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation -> e+1; (iv) same (save, epoch) -> identical draws.

## R14 Where the epoch lives and when it is durable (fixes kernel CR-15 vs SL-23 and the REBASED-key/trailer-SHA defect)
- `restore_epoch` is stored in a **per-slot side file** `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32), written atomically (temp file + rename) by the Save/Load worker. It is **not** in any generation file, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA and every key derived from them never change.
- When an advance is due (R13), Save/Load issues the epoch write in a **pre-restore staging step, before calling `request_restore`**, polls it per frame (never blocks the main thread), and calls `request_restore(gen, restore_epoch)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`. The kernel's LOADING stays atomic within one boundary service. Kernel CR-15 is reworded to: "Save/Load's epoch staging step has completed (EPOCH_DURABLE, or a logged SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE with save_status = FAILED)", and the kernel lists the failure-path exposure too.
- If the write fails or exceeds `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500 ms placeholder), the restore proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED` (the device is failing; saving is impossible anyway). This is a **listed exposure**: a kill before any later successful write may replay that epoch once. The ACs for durability are scoped to the success path; the failure path has its own AC (logged, status FAILED, play continues).
- A missing or corrupt `slot_epoch.bin` reads as `max(epoch recorded in the newest generation's header copy, 0) + 1`. Each generation header also records the epoch at write time (read-only copy, for recovery).

## R15 OQ-52: confirmed option (a)
A `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` is exempt from the fairness step-back. Confirmed; drop "USER DECISION".

## R16 OQ-DO-30: option (A)
The playtest preset registers only `debug_overlay_mark`; `debug_overlay_reveal` is dev-only. A tester session can never leave `HIDDEN`. Update DO-2/6/8, AC-DO-170, AC-DO-185.

## R17 Interaction OQ 48: confirmed
A wounded victim is not guaranteed an escape (Pillar 3, honest horror). Confirmed; no cooldown or damage floor.

## R18 Player Controller OQ 29(ii): pre-ruled conditional
If the target-acquisition spike fails and the lighter fallbacks do not close the gap, `aim_indicator` defaults ON for mouse players (still player-toggleable). Until then D9 (off by default) stands.

## R19 Boarding OQ-BS-34 fallback: pre-ruled conditional
If the boarding spike finds no K3 pass line inside 21-28 tiles with Attention's levers, the X3 route band's upper end widens to 31 tiles for the reference sortie (lower end stays 21). Not applied now; the spike decides.

## R20 Every "default applied, pending user confirmation" is confirmed
Every item marked "Default applied ... pending user confirmation" or "(confirm)" in any GDD is confirmed as of 2026-10-28 by delegation. Re-mark it "confirmed 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R20" and remove it from open user-decision lists. Do not change the value.

Any other "USER DECISION" left in a GDD is decided by its creative-director lean (G2) or, absent one, by the option that preserves prior user rulings and needs the least new content; record it as delegated ruling R21 with one sentence of reason. Never leave a "USER DECISION" open.

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). content.content:
# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria

Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.

- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

Which requests defer: (a) while `SAVING` is active (possible only from inside the capture) EVERY control-plane request is `DEFERRED`, as the SAVING cell already says; a deferred `request_restore` or `request_new_game` flushes the queue with `Dropped(RELOAD)` at the boundary where it is served. (b) while `LOADING` is active (possible only from inside `restore`, `default_state`, `init_world`, `post_restore` or a `binding_source` callback, which the contract forbids from side effects) only `request_shutdown` is `DEFERRED` (served at the boundary after the atomic step, CR-15); `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore` and `request_new_game` are `IGNORED`, each leaving one invalid-transition entry naming (`LOADING`, trigger). This matches Save/Load T-1 (a second request in LOADING is ignored and reported) and stops a deferred second restore from running a double reload. (c) A request made before the boundary service starts and sitting behind a restore in the same boundary's arrival order (for example the `request_pause` a requester queues after `request_restore`) is NOT made while LOADING: it is served in arrival order after `LOADING -> RUNNING` and before any tick, evaluated from `RUNNING`.

15	## Summary
16	
17	The Command & Simulation Layer is the thin kernel every other system runs inside: a fixed 60 Hz tick, a single door through which every change to the game's state passes as an authority-checked, peer-stamped **command**, a registry of **state blocks** that domain systems own and the kernel never does, and a once-per-tick **change notification** that presentation reads but can never write back through. The player never sees it; what they get from it is a ship that cannot lie — gauges and sprites may be hallucinated, but there is exactly one authoritative truth beneath them, and every command is judged against it. The kernel does not make that truth visible — how, when and at what cost the player learns why a command failed is priced by Interaction, Sanity and the HUD under Pillar 4's verification rule. It exists so that *The World Never Lies* and *Sanity Rewrites Reality* are structural rather than aspirational, and so that co-op can be added later without a rewrite: single-player is simply the host with one local peer.
18	
19	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Foundation` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `None` (upstream); 26 downstream systems named in the Dependencies table (23 hard — 16 with a systems-index edge, 7 presentation consumers whose edges are still to be added — and 3 soft), all MVP/VS systems register with or read it *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the earlier "16" counted only the hard rows that already had an index edge)*. **Section letters used throughout** (the template's order): A Overview, B Player Fantasy, C Detailed Design (C.3 = its Interactions table), D Formulas, E Edge Cases, F Dependencies, G Tuning Knobs, H Acceptance Criteria

21	## Overview
22	
23	The Command & Simulation Layer is the thin kernel every other system of The Synaptic Sea runs inside. It advances the simulation at a fixed tick, accepts every change to the game's state as a **command** carrying the identity of the peer that issued it, checks that peer's authority, validates the command against current state, applies it or rejects it with a reason, and then tells presentation what changed. It owns no domain state of its own: the Life-Support Graph, the ship layout, suit vitals, Attention, sanity and the rest each register their own **state block** with the kernel's registry and define their own command handlers. The kernel's job is to be the one door through which truth changes.
24	
25	The player never sees this system; they interact with it only through the systems built on it — every weld, every valve turned, every step taken is a command the kernel admitted. It is automatic from the player's point of view and invisible when it works.
26	
27	It exists for two reasons that are both pillars. First, **The World Never Lies** needs one authoritative truth: if any system could mutate state directly, two readers could disagree about whether a pipe is leaking, and the honest-world promise would be unenforceable. Second, **Sanity Rewrites Reality** needs a wall: the Perception Filter and every other presentation script may *read* simulation state and write only what is drawn, never what is true. The kernel is that wall made structural rather than aspirational, and its registry is also the hook the Save/Load contract and the true-value Debug Overlay hang from. The game would lose, without it, the ability to add co-op later without a rewrite (TD-FEASIBILITY: authority discipline from day one — in single-player the local peer simply *is* the host) and the guarantee that a hallucination can never corrupt the ship.
28	
29	**Design-level only.** Whether the kernel is an autoload, how commands are encoded, and how change notification is delivered are implementation choices → **becomes an ADR** (authority model). *(Framing: technical infrastructure, no ADR yet to cite, no direct player fantasy — selected as the recommended options for a `Core`/`Foundation` system under `autonomous` automation.)*
30	
31	## Player Fantasy
32	
33	*Indirect — the player never meets this system; they meet a promise it keeps.*
34	
35	**There is only one ship.** A gauge in the scrubber bay can read green while frost climbs the elbow beside it, and the player has to decide which to believe. The answer is always the same, and it is always available: the gauge and the frost both read the same state, and only one of them passed through the player's mind on the way to the screen. Nothing the player sees, hears or imagines can reach back and change what the ship is doing.
36	
37	The anchor moment is in the cryo bay or on the first sortie. The player has "fixed" a scrubber and the needle has settled. Then their breath fogs, and they realise the room is still getting colder. The horror is personal: *I am the thing that is broken.* The comfort is structural: *the ship is not.* Each time a player checks and the world turns out to be right, they learn to trust the world more and their own eyes less. That trust is the only thing this system gives the player, and one physical consequence that disagrees with what the ship is actually doing would spend it.
38	
39	In co-op, the same rule gives every act a name. A sane crewmate cannot fake the web's violence, and the beam in the corridor belongs to whoever's beam it is.
40	
41	**Pillars served.** *The World Never Lies*: "Pipes leak, frost forms, air hisses; the physical world is ground truth. Only instruments and perception can be wrong." *Sanity Rewrites Reality*: "Broken reads as fixed, fixed as broken; the lie extends from the gauge to the sprite. The physical consequence stays honest." The concept's own resolution of their tension — "the physical ship is ground truth; instruments and perception are what can be wrong. The tension is the game" — is what this kernel makes structurally true.
42	
43	**Design tests.**
44	- If we are debating whether a presentation-side effect (a hallucination, a light flicker, a UI animation) may adjust simulation state for convenience, or must be routed through a command: route it, or don't do it.
45	- The fantasy has failed if any player-visible physical consequence ever disagrees with the authoritative state. That is a Pillar 1 violation, not a cosmetic bug — and the reason the Debug Overlay exists.
46	
47	*What this section does not claim*: the kernel does not make the truth visible. Failure & Trail, Lighting's true reveal radius and the human channel do that. The kernel is why there is only one truth for them to show. (Alternatives considered: a co-op-first "identity behind every act" framing — true but untestable before VS-B and over-credits the kernel; a "steady pulse" fairness framing — honest about the tick but mostly the Graph's and Attention's fantasy.)
48	
49	## Detailed Design
50	
51	### Core Rules
52	
53	*Specialists consulted: systems-designer (primary), gameplay-programmer (feel/feasibility), engine-programmer (Godot 4.7.2 integration). Their one disagreement — tick rate — is resolved in CR-1. Items tagged **→ ADR** are engine-integration choices deliberately left out of this behaviour spec.*
54	
55	**Vocabulary.** *Tick*: one fixed-step iteration of the authoritative simulation; tick number `T` is a monotonically increasing integer and the only clock the simulation knows. *State block*: a named, versioned, single-owner container of domain state registered with the kernel. *Command*: a serializable request to change state, carrying issuer identity. *Owner*: the domain system that is the only writer of a block. *Read view*: the read-only accessor an owner publishes. *Step hook*: owner-registered code that runs in the propagation phase. *Mode*: `HOST` (authoritative; the only mode in MVP) or `MIRROR` (VS-B guest: receives state, runs no authoritative tick) — the public API is identical in both. *PlayerId*: a stable seat identity (1 in single-player; PlayerId 0 is reserved as "no seat" — additive, provisional *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics)*); *peer_id*: the transport identity of a connection (host = 1). Persistent per-player state is keyed by PlayerId, never by peer_id, because peer IDs are reassigned per connection (this corrects the systems index's "keyed by peer ID" for Sanity and Suit).
56	
57	**CR-1. Fixed tick at `TICK_RATE` = 60 Hz, with per-hook step divisors.** The simulation advances in steps of exactly `1/TICK_RATE` seconds of *simulated* time, independent of render frame time; durations everywhere are in ticks (the Attention tell window of 10–30 s is 600–1800 ticks). The kernel never reads wall-clock time or `delta`. Input- and physics-adjacent hooks run every tick; slow systems run at a divisor (Graph 6 → 10 Hz, Attention 6, Suit vitals 6, Sanity drift 12 → 5 Hz).
58	*Rationale and alternatives.* The gameplay-programmer argued for a 20 Hz kernel (slow systems don't need more; worst-case 50 ms latency is invisible behind immediate local acknowledgement) but set a hard floor of 15 Hz and would push back at 10. The engine-programmer argued for tick = physics rate so the moving ship body and the characters inside it share one timeline (*historical*: CR-1a later settled that the tick is driven from `_process`, not the physics step, and Body integrates ship-local kinematics inside the sim, so physics alignment is no longer a reason for any `TICK_RATE`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. 60 Hz + divisors satisfies both: one clock, submit-to-applied within one tick (16.7 ms of simulated time) on an empty queue, and the cost profile of a 10 Hz graph. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A variable timestep was rejected (breaks replay, tests and save equivalence); a 30 Hz kernel sits at a 2:1 ratio to the 60 fps render rate (alternate frames run 0 and 1 ticks), not at an awkward one to the physics step, which is not the clock. The tick *source* is settled in CR-1a (a `TickDriver` with an injected delta, not the physics callback); `step()` stays a plain method that tests and a future server call directly. Changing `TICK_RATE` later invalidates every tuned value expressed in ticks. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
59	
60	**CR-1a. Tick driver, clock source and catch-up** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; closes former Open Question 2, the technical-director confirms it in the spike)*. `Kernel.step()` has no clock. A `TickDriver` (a `RefCounted`, no scene tree) owns the accumulator, receives time as an injected integer count of microseconds (`delta_us`), and is driven by exactly one node with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` from its `_process(delta)`; that node converts the engine's `delta` to `delta_us` once, and that conversion plus the diagnostics timer are the only wall-clock reads in the project (H9). **Godot's physics step is not the clock**: at MVP the avatar has no physics body (CR-13), so nothing needs the physics callback, and the driver needs no coupling to `physics/common/max_physics_steps_per_frame` (the former coupled constraint 4 is deleted). A later Vertical Slice physics projection runs in `_physics_process` as a `PROJECTOR` reading committed state and never steps the kernel. The accumulator is an integer in units of *microseconds × TICK_RATE*, so one tick is exactly `TICK_UNITS` = 1,000,000 units for every integer `TICK_RATE` (no float drift, no boundary flips); each frame that begins (after the boundary service) with the kernel `RUNNING` adds `acc += delta_us × TICK_RATE`. **Order of the add against the clear** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the boundary service runs first; if it moved the kernel into `RUNNING` (a resume, a load, a finished save) the accumulator is cleared and **that frame's own `delta_us` is discarded** — the frame runs 0 ticks, because its wall time was spent paused, loading or saving — and the add applies from the next frame on; a frame that finds the kernel not `RUNNING` adds nothing. Per frame the driver (1) runs the boundary service (CR-15) before any tick; (2) while the kernel is `RUNNING`, runs `step()` `ticks_run = min(floor(acc / TICK_UNITS), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME)` times, **re-reading the kernel state after every `step()`** and stopping (and clearing `acc`) the moment it is no longer `RUNNING` — a P6 pause, a restore, a fault; (3) applies lag forgiveness (D.5); (4) flushes the result buffer (CR-5); (5) while `PAUSED`, runs the paused boundary service (CR-16). **The accumulator is cleared on every transition into `RUNNING`** (from `LOADING`, `PAUSED` or `SAVING`), so a load, an autosave or a pause never produces catch-up ticks afterwards. The driver node has a process priority that runs it before the presentation nodes, so presentation reads the tick the driver just produced. **Step 0 — input sample, and the priority table** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: nothing in the driver's step list sampled input, so the best-case latency of D.4 rested on an unstated ordering. The order inside one rendered frame is now fixed by process priority (lower runs first): **(0)** the input adapter (an `INPUT_SURFACE` object; it reads the engine's input state for this frame and calls `submit`, so its commands are admitted before the boundary service and the tick loop); **(1)** the `TickDriver` node (boundary service, then the tick loop, then forgiveness, result flush, paused service); **(2)** presentation nodes (Pixel-Perfect pipeline, HUD, Lighting, Audio), which read what the driver just committed. The adapter's priority is therefore strictly below the driver's number; a presentation node must sort after the driver (a lint on `process_priority` values; the engine reference is silent on ordering between nodes, so the spike verifies it, KRN-LAT-02). Tests call `Kernel.step()` directly, or inject `delta_us` into the driver; nothing in the kernel sleeps or reads a clock. **Main thread and `Engine.time_scale`**: the kernel, the driver and every owner callable run on the main thread only — no worker thread calls `submit`, a read view or a mutator (a lint forbids `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool` and `call_deferred` into kernel code); `_process(delta)`'s `delta` is scaled by `Engine.time_scale` in the engine's contract as we read it (the pinned engine reference does not state it — **[UNV]**, verify in the spike), so release builds pin `Engine.time_scale = 1.0` (a boot check records `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT` in diagnostics otherwise) and a dev build that changes it knowingly scales simulated speed through `delta` — ticks stay exact integers either way.
61	
62	**CR-2. Tick phase order.** Each tick executes these phases to completion, in order, with no interleaving:
63	
64	| # | Phase | What happens | Who may write blocks |
65	|---|-------|--------------|----------------------|
66	| P0 | Begin | Tick counter increments; the pending set is *frozen* as this tick's candidate set (commands arriving now wait for T+1) | nobody |
67	| P1 | Intake | Candidate set in ordering-key order (CR-13) — a sort only when a non-monotone (remote) insert happened since the last tick, otherwise the head of an already-ordered queue — the first `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` form this tick's **batch**; the overflow returns to the unfrozen pending set in order and stays supersedable (Section E) | nobody |
68	| P2 | Dispatch | Per command in order: authority check → validate → apply or reject (CR-5) | the handler, inside `apply` only |
69	| P3 | Step | Step hooks in resolved order (CR-3); a hook runs when `T mod divisor == offset` | the hook's own block, plus owner-published mutators of other blocks (CR-9) |
70	| P4 | Commit | Dirty sets finalised; "tick committed" marker advances; interpolation baseline captured (`commit_baseline()` on each `interpolated` block — a kernel-run roll of a **derived presentation cache**, not a block write: the baseline is excluded from `snapshot()`, `canonical_bytes` and every hash, and is rebuilt by `snap_baseline` on every transition into `RUNNING`, so it has no canonical status and "nobody writes" stays true) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | nobody |
71	| P5 | Notify | Batched change notifications delivered (CR-10), then the result buffer is flushed (CR-5) | nobody — writes disabled |
72	| P6 | Boundary services | Pending control-plane requests in arrival order (CR-15), pending snapshot (Saving), command-log append | the kernel only |
73	
74	P2 commands see earlier P2 effects in the same tick; P3 sees all of P2; subscribers and presentation only ever see post-P4 state, never a half-applied tick. **Paused service cycle** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; a retained seam that only test fixtures exercise at MVP, because no MVP command type sets `allowed_when_paused`)*: on every rendered frame while `PAUSED` the driver runs the paused boundary service — P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 with no P0 and no P3, `T` unchanged — dispatching only commands of `allowed_when_paused` types (CR-16). It is a deliberate carve-out from the running-tick guarantees: its commits apply at the current `T` (`apply_tick == queued_tick` is legal there, unlike a running tick), several commits can share one `T`, and G1/G2/G3 hold for it only as CR-13 states.
75	
76	**CR-3. Step hooks and ordering.** Hooks register `(hook_id, owner, divisor, offset, after: [hook_id | {hook_id, tolerates_stale}])`. The kernel resolves a total order by topological sort of `after`; ties break by registration order, then `hook_id`. A cycle or unknown `hook_id` fails boot (CR-6). Sim-to-sim data flow within a tick is "reader declares `after` writer" (Suit vitals `after: graph.propagate.atmo` — the Graph registers three chained hooks, see its LS-1 *(Amended 2026-10-26 — consistency check, routed from the Life-Support Graph GDD)*). The order is data: testable, and printable by the Debug Overlay. An `after` edge between two hooks that never run in the same tick (Section E) must carry `tolerates_stale: true` if the reader accepts data up to a divisor old; boot warns only for **undeclared** mismatches, so the real boot (`horror.step` divisor 5 after `attention.step` divisor 6, the Graph's staggered chain — `.atmo` (6, 2) after `.power` (6, 0), `.failure` (6, 4) after `.atmo` — and the other cross-offset pairs of Section E) stays silent once declared and the warning keeps its meaning *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Hooks may not submit `PLAYER`-origin commands; they may submit `SYSTEM`-origin ones (CR-4) through `submit_system(type, payload, dedupe_key = none)` and may ask `has_pending(type, dedupe_key)` (CR-9 owner rule).
77	
78	**CR-4. Command anatomy, origin and intents.** A command is plain serializable data:
79	
80	| Field | Meaning |
81	|-------|---------|
82	| `type` | Registered command type ID, owned by a domain system |
83	| `issuer_peer` | Stamped by the kernel's ingress — never taken from the payload |
84	| `origin` | `PLAYER` or `SYSTEM`, stamped by ingress |
85	| `actor` | The entity the command acts as: an opaque ID in the ID space of the type's declared `actor_source` block (CR-7; IDs are block-local, CR-8, so one number can name different entities in two blocks), or none *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
86	| `seq` | Monotonically increasing integer per `(issuer_peer, origin)` — the host's `PLAYER` and `SYSTEM` streams are separate spaces *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **Stamped by the kernel at ISSUED, never chosen by a local caller**: every local `INPUT_SURFACE` handle and `submit_system()` receives the next value of the one kernel-held counter for its `(issuer_peer, origin)`, so any number of surfaces sharing the `(1, PLAYER)` space can never collide; the counter advances on every submit, including one rejected at admission, so locally stamped values are dense (1, 2, 3 …) and `DUPLICATE_SEQ` and gap counting apply only to a `seq` supplied by the **test ingress or a remote ingress** (the only two callers that may supply one) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)* |
87	| `correlation` | Optional opaque `int` the submitting caller attaches (default 0 = none); the kernel never interprets it and echoes it unchanged in the command's result record and in any rejection event, so a caller (the Player Controller's pre-play tokens, a menu) matches a result to the act that caused it without learning or choosing `seq`. Kernel metadata like `submission_id`, never payload-borne; not part of `canonical_bytes` or any hash. Not unique: two submits may carry the same `correlation` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)* |
88	| `payload` | Plain data only, per the recursive whitelist below; no object references, node paths or callables; `var_to_bytes(payload, false).size()` ≤ `MAX_PAYLOAD` |
89	| `queued_tick` | Stamped on enqueue |
90	| `submission_id` | Kernel metadata, never payload-borne: a kernel-unique counter stamped at ISSUED, before admission, so even a rejected submit has one; it is the `result_id` of the command's result (CR-5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
91	
92	*Discrete commands vs continuous intents.* If the sim must log, validate, save or replay it, it is a command (examples; each type's owner GDD is authoritative: Controller `set_move_intent`, `set_aim`, `toggle_beam`; Interaction `begin_cut` (module salvage, V8), `begin_patch`, `cancel_channel`, `pickup`, `drop`, `set_switch`, `field_check`; Modular Ship Assembly `begin_weld` (declared by Interaction, registered by Assembly), `begin_seam_cut`, `install_module` and the `SYSTEM`-only completions `weld` / `seam_cut` (registry: `assembly_commands`; there is no `remove_module` — it is reserved and unregistered, and V8 salvage is the only removal); Suit `equip_tool` (its only type); Web Map & Transit `pod_hop`, `berth`, `unberth` and the `SYSTEM`-only `pod_arrive`, `pod_settle`, `berth_step`, `web_reconcile` (registry: `web_commands`). `interact` is an input action, not a command type, and `use_item` has no owner and is not a command *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from interaction-system, suit-and-equipment, modular-ship-assembly and web-map-and-transit)*). What the stick is doing *right now* is an intent: intents are commands too, but a type may declare `coalesce = LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK` — coalescing happens at admission over the unfrozen queue, keyed `(type, actor, issuer_peer)`, the older command becoming `Superseded` — and the input adapter sends one only when the quantised value changes — a few per second, never one per tick. Edge-triggered inputs (press, release, confirm) must declare `coalesce = NONE` or taps are lost. Movement integration runs inside the sim: Body's `body.integrate` hook (divisor 1, P3) reads the current intent and integrates ship-local kinematics (CR-13), so a move intent takes effect one tick after it is submitted, like every command; there is no physics-side integration at MVP, and position ownership is settled (Body owns it; the Controller owns intent and facing) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Under `STRICT_DEBUG` every command is round-tripped through serialization before dispatch, even locally; one that cannot survive is a violation (CR-19). **Submit is fire-and-forget and never calls back**: `submit()` returns nothing and invokes no callback, handler or subscriber, so it is safe to call from any handler, hook or result handler; its only outcome is one result record appended to the kernel's result buffer (CR-5), delivered at the next flush and identified by `result_id` — a remote issuer could never get a synchronous answer, so the local one doesn't either *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. `submit()` takes the optional `correlation` and returns nothing, not even a receipt: the caller learns the outcome only from the result record, which carries its `correlation` back, so "fire-and-forget" is literally true and `seq` stays the kernel's. The API shape is `submit(type, payload, actor = none, correlation = 0)` on an `INPUT_SURFACE` handle and `submit_system(type, payload, dedupe_key = none)` for hooks (a hook needs no correlation: it never receives a result) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)*.
93	
94	**Payload whitelist** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. 'Plain' is a recursive `Variant.Type` whitelist checked at admission: `NIL`, `BOOL`, `INT`, `FLOAT` (finite only — `NaN` and `±inf` are `MALFORMED`; the same finite check applies to **each component of a `VECTOR2` and each element of `PackedFloat32Array`, `PackedFloat64Array` and `PackedVector2Array`**, which the walk visits in O(n) bounded by `MAX_PAYLOAD` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), `STRING`, `STRING_NAME`, `VECTOR2`, `VECTOR2I`, the `Packed{Byte,Int32,Int64,Float32,Float64,String,Vector2}Array` types, and `ARRAY`/`DICTIONARY` of the same, to a depth cap `PAYLOAD_MAX_DEPTH` = 8 (which also rejects a self-containing container). Dictionary keys must be `INT`, `STRING` or `STRING_NAME` and **all keys of one dictionary must share one type** (mixed keys have no canonical order, D.12). Anything else — an `Object`, `NodePath`, `Callable`, `Signal`, `RID`, a non-whitelisted `Variant.Type`, a non-finite float, a depth-9 nesting, mixed dictionary keys — is `MALFORMED`; the size bound is measured as `var_to_bytes(payload, false).size()` after the walk passes. Immediate *acknowledgement* (a tool sound, a hand animation, a linear progress bar starting) is presentation's job and happens in the same frame; the sim confirms on the next tick. The latency bounds are stated once, in Game Feel and D.4.
95	
96	**CR-5. Command lifecycle and the exactly-one-result guarantee.** Every command reaches exactly one terminal state and emits exactly one result record (identified by `result_id`; delivered to its issuer unless it is `SYSTEM`-origin, see Result identity and delivery below). Stages: *Issued* → *Admission* (kernel state accepts commands; type registered; **origin allowed for the type — known at admission, so rejected there**; queue not full; `seq` not a duplicate — gaps are accepted and counted, not rejected; issuer rate limit; payload plain) → *Queued* → *Authority check* in P2 (origin re-checked as a defence in depth; if the type declares `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, the binding table says the issuer controls the key `(actor_source, actor)` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; age ≤ the type's `max_age_ticks`) → *Validate* (owner's side-effect-free `validate(cmd, views, ctx)`: it reports through `ctx.ok()` or `ctx.reject(reason)` — a domain reason — and ends with `return ctx.complete()`; its return value carries no outcome, CR-19(a)/(b)) → *Apply* (`apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx)`, ending with `return ctx.complete()`; infallible by contract once validate passed, CR-9) → terminal: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R3)*
97	
98	| Terminal | Meaning |
99	|----------|---------|
100	| `Applied` | Effects are in state as of tick T (a command dispatched earlier in a tick that then faults is still `Applied`, with `detail.uncommitted = 1`) |
101	| `Rejected(reason)` | No effect |
102	| `Dropped(reason)` | Never evaluated: a reload, a shutdown or a fault flushed it — `RELOAD`, `SHUTDOWN`, `FAULTED` (the last added so G5 holds on the defect path). Includes the not-yet-dispatched commands of a faulting tick's batch *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
103	| `Faulted(code)` | Evaluated, and its `validate` or `apply` (or a mutator it called) reported a fault through the fault channel (CR-19): effects may be partial and are unreachable to presentation. Exactly one command per fault — the cause. Distinct from `Rejected` (not 'no effect') and `Dropped` (not 'never evaluated') *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
104	| `Superseded` | Coalesced away by a newer command of a coalescing type |
105	
106	Kernel reject reasons are a closed set: `NOT_ACCEPTING`, `PAUSED`, `UNKNOWN_TYPE`, `QUEUE_FULL`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `DUPLICATE_SEQ`, `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`, `STALE`, `MALFORMED`, `VALIDATION_FAILED(domain_code)` — domain codes are namespaced and owned by the registering system (Interaction's set, e.g. `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `INVALID_TARGET`, `PRECONDITION`, `BUSY`, is its GDD's). The result record carries `result_id`, `issuer_peer`, `origin`, `seq`, `correlation`, `ok`, `reason`, `subject` (the target the rejection refers to), an optional `detail` dictionary of numbers, and `tick` — **never display strings** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `result_id` and `origin` added)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2: `correlation` added, echoed unchanged from the submit)*. Presentation maps reasons to sound, shake or tooltip. **Reason codes are computed from true state and the kernel never filters them.** That is the whole of the kernel's claim. Whether, when and how cheaply a reason reaches the player is *not* the kernel's: Interaction, Sanity and the HUD own it and must obey Pillar 4's cost rule (a check costs time, risk or trust) — for example surfacing a `PRECONDITION` only after channel time has been spent, or only through diegetic feedback rather than an instant tooltip. *Design test (CD-GDD-ALIGN):* if a rejection lets the player falsify a hallucination at zero time, risk or trust cost, the presentation of that rejection is wrong — not the kernel. A command *aborted mid-channel* (power drops during a cut) is reported by the channel owner through state change, not through the command result. The kernel never retries.
107	
108	**Result identity and delivery** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A result is identified by `result_id` (the command's `submission_id`). A local issuer correlates by the `correlation` it attached to the submit (echoed unchanged; the caller's own uniqueness, not the kernel's), never by `seq`, which a local caller neither chooses nor learns *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)*. `(issuer_peer, origin, seq)` is unique among results **except** `DUPLICATE_SEQ` rejections, which by definition repeat an earlier command's `(issuer_peer, origin, seq)` and are told apart by `result_id` and `reason`; only a test or remote ingress can produce one (see the `seq` row of CR-4). Every terminal result — admission rejections, `Superseded`, P2 results, `Dropped(...)`, `Faulted` — is appended to the kernel's **result buffer** in the order it occurs; `submit()` itself never delivers. The buffer is flushed (a) at P5 of every tick, after the change batch, and (b) by the driver once per rendered frame after that frame's ticks, **in every kernel state** (`BOOTING`, `LOADING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `FAULTED`, `SHUTTING_DOWN`, and an idle frame with no tick), so `NOT_ACCEPTING`, `PAUSED`, `Dropped(RELOAD|SHUTDOWN|FAULTED)` and every other result always have a delivery point. A flush swaps the buffer out before delivering: whatever a result handler submits (the STALE resubmit of Section E, for example) is admitted normally, and any result it produces lands in the fresh buffer and is delivered at the next flush, never recursively — a handler that resubmits on every rejection costs one result per flush and cannot loop. Results go to the issuing `INPUT_SURFACE`'s result handler and to the diagnostics log. **`SYSTEM`-origin results are never delivered to a subscriber or to the submitting owner** (owners never subscribe, CR-10); they go to the command log and the diagnostics counters only, and an owner that needs the outcome reads state. **Fault semantics (a designer decision, not an implementer detail)**: when the kernel faults, each command already dispatched in the faulting tick whose `apply` completed receives `Applied` with `detail.uncommitted = 1` (its effects are in the live blocks although P4 never ran); the faulting command receives `Faulted(code)`; every not-yet-dispatched batch command and every pending command receives `Dropped(FAULTED)`; all are buffered at the fault transition and delivered at the next frame flush.
109	
110	**CR-6. Registration at boot, then frozen.** Block, command-type, hook, diagnostics-channel and binding-source registration are legal only in `BOOTING` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from debug-overlay-true-values (E-DO-38))* (a block may declare one optional `binding_source` callable, CR-7; one registered after `BOOTING` is refused like every other registration *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*); after `BOOTING → LOADING` the registries are immutable until shutdown. Registration is an explicit declaration by the composition root, not discovery via the scene tree. Duplicate IDs, unknown types, missing owners and hook cycles fail boot loudly in every build. A command type registered without `allowed_origins`, `actor_binding`, `coalesce` or `max_age_ticks` (**no silent defaults**: an omitted `actor_binding` must never mean 'no ownership check'), a type with `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER` but no `actor_source`, one whose `actor_source` names a block that registered no `binding_source`, and a `NONE` type that declares an `actor_source` (each fails boot with `ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID`, naming the type) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, a block registered without `class`, `gameplay`, `repl_hint` or `persist`, a type whose `writes_blocks` names an unregistered block, and an `allowed_when_paused` type whose `writes_blocks` names any `gameplay = true` block likewise fail boot (`BOOTING → FAULTED`) naming the registration. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A type with `coalesce ≠ NONE` that allows both origins fails boot (`COALESCE_DUAL_ORIGIN`), because the supersession key carries no origin (D.8); and the joint memory assertion of Section G constraint 8 is checked here *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.

395	**Output Range:** At the default, `lag_ticks == 0` after every frame, so the player never sees fast-forward: a frame that runs more than one tick does so only to cover wall time that elapsed within that one frame (at most `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME`), never to repay lag from an earlier frame. Sustained frame times above `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME × tick_duration` (66.7 ms) run the sim at `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` ticks per frame — slow motion, no spiral. Since no domain system reads wall time, dropped time is observable only in diagnostics. The earlier text allowed up to 30 ticks of sub-threshold lag to be repaid at up to 4× for up to 10 frames; that allowance is withdrawn. For a fixture with `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS = N > 0` the most repayment is `N` ticks over `ceil(N / (MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME − 1))` frames.
396	**Example (default, hitch):** a 1.000 s hitch: `acc += 60,000,000` → `ticks_run = 4`, `lag_ticks = 56 > 0` → forgiven the same frame: `dropped = 56`, `lag_ticks = 0`, `acc = 0`; the next 16,667 µs frame (`acc = 1,000,020`) runs exactly 1 tick and leaves `acc = 20`.

The next 16,667 µs frame: `acc = 1,120,020` → `ticks_run = 1`, `acc = 120,020`. No frame after the hitch runs more than 1 tick.

I'm still working through this: stopping as soon as it's no longer RUNNING fails to catch atomic transitions that return to RUNNING. A restore mid-loop at tick 1 of 4 lets ticks 2-4 proceed on the freshly loaded world, and the accumulator ends up negative since it's cleared then subtracted from again.

Autosave transitioning SAVING back to RUNNING mid-loop has the same problem — clearing the accumulator partway through and then subtracting makes it negative, which starves later frames since ticks_due and ticks_run floor on negatives. This is a genuine implementability gap showing up for the third review in a row, and tracing when the driver actually serves a snapshot request mid-loop (e.g. a death restore triggered from a Body hook at P6 of a tick) confirms it's a realistic, not just theoretical, scenario.

Severity-wise, it's still implementation-level rather than impossible, so I'll keep it RECOMMENDED but flag that it's been carried across three reviews now. Tags and bodies — `0x00 NIL` (no body); `0x01 BOOL` (1 byte, 0 or 1); `0x02 INT` (8 bytes, little-endian two's complement); `0x03 FLOAT` (8 bytes, the IEEE-754 bit pattern, little-endian, with `−0.0 → +0.0` and every NaN → `0x7FF8000000000000`); `0x04 STRING` (u64 little-endian UTF-8 byte length, then the bytes) — **a `StringName` is encoded as the `STRING` of its text**, so equal text is equal bytes; `0x05 VECTOR2` (two normalised `FLOAT` bodies, 16 bytes, no inner tags); `0x06 VECTOR2I` (two 8-byte little-endian ints, sign-extended, 16 bytes); `0x07 ARRAY` (u64 element **count**, then that many tagged values, in order); `0x08 DICT` (u64 entry **count**, then `key, value` tagged pairs sorted bytewise by the **encoded key bytes**; all keys of one dictionary share one type, CR-4); `0x09 PACKED` (one element-type byte, u64 element count, then the raw little-endian element bytes; a `PackedStringArray` element is a u64 length plus UTF-8, a `PackedVector2Array` element is two 4-byte floats). I'm checking the KRN-BND-01 and KRN-PERF-04 findings against the queue capacity and payload size numbers to verify they're consistent with the stated budgets.

I'm also sweeping through the remaining checkboxes — test seams, review-class items, and the spike-gated or intentionally untestable entries — to flag which pass lines are missing versus which are deliberately withdrawn, and confirming the Save/Load timing and empty-queue scenarios look plausible.

But I'm catching a deeper inconsistency: if a duplicate block-ID registration faults boot immediately into FAULTED, then the legal FAULTED→LOADING transition via request_new_game could let a user re-enter LOADING with a registry that was never properly frozen or validated, since that exit path is meant for explicit user recovery, not necessarily for a broken registry state.

So a user could click New campaign again after a boot fault, triggering request_new_game from FAULTED into LOADING with an invalid registry — this seems like a genuinely new gap. I'll recommend adding a rule that a registry-validation FAULTED state is terminal, and that restore/new-game requests in it should be ignored with a boot-registry error.

I should also check the ordering concern around when request_new_game gets called relative to Save/Load's new_game(world_seed) and composition root completion, plus the boot-cycle validation rules in CR-6. content.content: **CR-15. Control plane** (host-local, not commands): `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; CR-18)*, `request_shutdown`. Callers: Save/Load, the pause/Chart Table UI (host-local call), boot code. **Timing** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a request is recorded when made — from any phase, from a hook, from a P5 handler, or from outside a tick (a UI call between frames) — and served at the **next boundary**, where a boundary is the P6 of a tick or the driver's per-frame boundary service (run before any tick of the frame and, while `PAUSED`, every frame), whichever comes first; the call itself never changes state. `request_shutdown` is accepted from **every state except `SHUTTING_DOWN`** (including `BOOTING`, `LOADING` and `SAVING`; in those it is served at the boundary that follows the atomic step). Requests reaching the same boundary are applied in arrival order, never coalesced: a `request_pause` then a `request_resume` on one boundary leaves the kernel `RUNNING` with no paused service cycle run; a caller that needs a definite state re-issues the state it wants (Chart Table CT-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from chart-table-web-map-and-menus (ASK-CT-9))*. **`request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash = none)`** (K-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1; amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14: `restore_epoch` is supplied by Save/Load, whose epoch staging step has completed before the call is made: `EPOCH_DURABLE`, or a logged `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` with `save_status = FAILED`, or no advance was due. Save/Load advances the value on every death-stub restore, every `FAULT_RECOVERY` and every Continue except one of the newest non-demoted verified `QUIT` generation, which carries it unchanged and writes nothing (R13). The kernel never waits on that write: no Save/Load I/O completes inside `LOADING`, which stays atomic within one boundary service (States). **Listed exposure (failure path, R14):** after `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` the installed epoch exists only in Save/Load's memory, so a process kill before Save/Load's next successful epoch write may replay that epoch once; G3/G4 are unaffected because they are defined given the `(save bytes, restore_epoch)` pair. The kernel holds it read-only for the session, exposes it in the `kernel.clock` read view (CR-8) and rejects a value outside the u32 range in its pre-check, `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE`)*: when an expected hash is given, the kernel recomputes `state_hash(PERSIST, T)` (D.12) after the last `post_restore()`, inside `LOADING` and before the first `RUNNING` tick, and reports `{T, computed_hash, match}` to the requester; Save/Load derives its EXACT / REBASED / mismatch verdict from it (SL-12). A mismatch is **not** a `FAULTED` transition — release plays on; policy is the requester's. Save/Load does not use restore-into-`PAUSED` for this window *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (K-4))*. **Control-plane read access:** a control-plane caller is not one of the CR-10 subscriber classes; Save/Load (the one such caller at MVP) may read `kernel.clock`, the Controller's per-seat `loco_state`, the Graph's `read_view.failures()` and an optional Attention `SIM` read view, and receives end-of-tick notifications, all read in the tick boundary in which it issues a request; it never reads `PERCEPTION_OUT`, never submits commands and never holds a `WriteScope` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (SL-13))*. In VS-B a guest's pause or save *request* is a command defined by Session or Save/Load, validated on the host, which then calls the control API.

findings.section: CR-1a / D.5 / AC L907 (carried over from reviews 4 and 5, G3: not fixed in three passes)
findings.finding: SAVING and LOADING are atomic within one boundary service and return to RUNNING before the driver re-reads state. The driver loop (CR-1a step 2) says it stops 'the moment it is no longer RUNNING', but a death-stub restore served at the P6 of tick 1 of a 4-tick catch-up frame leaves the kernel RUNNING. Ticks 2-4 then run on the freshly loaded world. CR-1a also clears acc on every transition into RUNNING, and D.5 then subtracts ticks_run x TICK_UNITS from it, so acc goes negative (D.5 gives its range as 0 to unbounded). A negative acc makes floor(acc/TICK_UNITS) negative and starves later frames. L907 only covers a restore served in the boundary service before any tick.
findings.fix: Give the kernel a monotonic transition counter (or a restore_or_save_served flag) that the driver compares after every step(). When it changes, the driver clears acc, sets ticks_run to the ticks actually stepped, skips the subtraction, runs no further tick this frame, and skips forgiveness. Add D.5 acc >= 0 as an invariant and an AC: restore requested in a hook of tick 1 of a 4-tick frame gives exactly 1 tick that frame and acc == 0. Do the same for an autosave (SAVING) served mid-loop.

findings.section: States and Transitions L171/L183/L196 (new gap exposed by the first-boot rows)
findings.finding: A registry-validation failure (hook cycle, unknown dependency, ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID, MAX_BLOCKS) puts the kernel in FAULTED. L196 says FAULTED request_restore / request_new_game goes to LOADING, 'the only exits other than shutdown'. The Chart Table FAULTED-return menu offers New campaign again, so a second request_new_game from a boot-faulted kernel is a tabled transition into LOADING with an invalid, unfrozen registry. KRN-STATE-03 only covers the first request ('the request is not honoured'). E-section text says 'No partial order is ever used'.
findings.fix: State that a FAULTED entered from BOOTING (registry or registration failure) is terminal: request_restore and request_new_game are IGNORED there, with one invalid-transition entry carrying a BOOT_REGISTRY_INVALID reason, and only request_shutdown exits. Add one clause to KRN-STATE-03 and the FAULTED row at L196.

findings.section: L199 / KRN-STATE-01 (L913) vs the new DEFERRED/IGNORED model (L201, KRN-STATE-04)
findings.finding: L199 still says 'every other (state, trigger) pair is invalid: ignored, one invalid-transition entry', and KRN-STATE-01 asserts that every unlisted pair leaves exactly one invalid-transition entry. But (SAVING, any request) is now DEFERRED and later SERVED, and (LOADING, request_shutdown) is DEFERRED. Neither is in the transition table or invalid. A table-driven fixture generated from the tables cannot satisfy both. The 'pair count' note in the registry entry control_plane_request_outcomes (BOOTING rows add 2) is also not reflected anywhere in the GDD text. KRN-STATE-04 asserts DEFERRED and IGNORED, but nothing asserts SERVED, and the diagnostics-surface AC (L1079) does not list the outcome log.
findings.fix: Change L199 and KRN-STATE-01 to: the SAVING pairs are DEFERRED (not invalid), (LOADING, request_shutdown) is DEFERRED, and the other LOADING pairs are IGNORED. Add one fixture row per outcome class, assert SERVED for each tabled transition, and add the outcome log to the L1079 diagnostics-surface list. Request the Debug Overlay counter or reader if it is wanted.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs L798/L799/L804/L815 + constraints 1 and 8 + KRN-BND-01 (carried over)
findings.finding: Several 'safe' ranges break coupled constraints at their own ends. MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK = 32 with the default QUEUE_CAPACITY 1024 gives a drain of 32 ticks, above the 30-tick intent max_age_ticks (constraint 1 fails). QUEUE_CAPACITY = 3840 (the stated ceiling) at MAX_PAYLOAD 4 KiB needs 3840 x 4296 B + 4.1 MiB log, about 19.8 MiB, which exceeds the 16 MiB default budget (constraint 8 fails). MAX_PAYLOAD = 64 KiB fails constraint 8 even at the default queue. COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET = 8 MiB is inside its range, but the defaults need 4.195 + 4.098 = 8.29 MiB, so the range minimum fails the defaults. The table says '8.5 MiB (4.2 + 4.3)' (4.3 is MB, the log is 4.1 MiB) and KRN-BND-01 says 'about 8.5 MiB'.
findings.fix: Restate every range as conditional on constraints 1 and 8 (as QUEUE_CAPACITY already is for constraint 1), or tighten the numeric ranges so each end boots. Set the budget floor at 9 MiB (or the formula) and use one unit (MiB) with the arithmetic 4.195 + 4.098 = 8.29 MiB. Fix the KRN-BND-01 text, and add a boundary AC for MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK = 32.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria L1076 (KRN H1 lint) and CR-14 H1 (carried over)

findings.section: CR-1a / D.5 / AC L907 (carried over from reviews 4 and 5, G3: not fixed in three passes)
findings.finding: SAVING and LOADING are atomic within one boundary service and return to RUNNING before the driver re-reads state. The driver loop (CR-1a step 2) says it stops 'the moment it is no longer RUNNING', but a death-stub restore served at the P6 of tick 1 of a 4-tick catch-up frame leaves the kernel RUNNING. Ticks 2-4 then run on the freshly loaded world. CR-1a also clears acc on every transition into RUNNING, and D.5 then subtracts ticks_run x TICK_UNITS from it, so acc goes negative (D.5 gives its range as 0 to unbounded). A negative acc makes floor(acc/TICK_UNITS) negative and starves later frames. L907 only covers a restore served in the boundary service before any tick.
findings.fix: Give the kernel a monotonic transition counter (or a restore_or_save_served flag) that the driver compares after every step(). When it changes, the driver clears acc, sets ticks_run to the ticks actually stepped, skips the subtraction, runs no further tick this frame, and skips forgiveness. Add D.5 acc >= 0 as an invariant and an AC: restore requested in a hook of tick 1 of a 4-tick frame gives exactly 1 tick that frame and acc == 0. Do the same for an autosave (SAVING) served mid-loop.

KRN-STATE-03 only covers the first request ('the request is not honoured'). E-section text says 'No partial order is ever used'.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs L798/L799/L804/L815 + constraints 1 and 8 + KRN-BND-01 (carried over)
findings.finding: Several 'safe' ranges break coupled constraints at their own ends. MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK = 32 with the default QUEUE_CAPACITY 1024 gives a drain of 32 ticks, above the 30-tick intent max_age_ticks (constraint 1 fails). QUEUE_CAPACITY = 3840 (the stated ceiling) at MAX_PAYLOAD 4 KiB needs 3840 x 4296 B + 4.1 MiB log, about 19.8 MiB, which exceeds the 16 MiB default budget (constraint 8 fails). MAX_PAYLOAD = 64 KiB fails constraint 8 even at the default queue. COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET = 8 MiB is inside its range, but the defaults need 4.195 + 4.098 = 8.29 MiB, so the range minimum fails the defaults. findings.fix: Restate every range as conditional on constraints 1 and 8 (as QUEUE_CAPACITY already is for constraint 1), or tighten the numeric ranges so each end boots.
