Add D.5 acc >= 0 as an invariant and an AC: restore requested in a hook of tick 1 of a 4-tick frame gives exactly 1 tick that frame and acc == 0. Do the same for an autosave (SAVING) served mid-loop.

findings.section: States and Transitions L171/L183/L196 (new gap exposed by the first-boot rows)
findings.finding: A registry-validation failure (hook cycle, unknown dependency, ACTOR_SOURCE_INVALID, MAX_BLOCKS) puts the kernel in FAULTED. L196 says FAULTED request_restore / request_new_game goes to LOADING, 'the only exits other than shutdown'. The Chart Table FAULTED-return menu offers New campaign again, so a second request_new_game from a boot-faulted kernel is a tabled transition into LOADING with an invalid, unfrozen registry. KRN-STATE-03 only covers the first request ('the request is not honoured'). E-section text says 'No partial order is ever used'.
findings.fix: State that a FAULTED entered from BOOTING (registry or registration failure) is terminal: request_restore and request_new_game are IGNORED there, with one invalid-transition entry carrying a BOOT_REGISTRY_INVALID reason, and only request_shutdown exits. Add one clause to KRN-STATE-03 and the FAULTED row at L196.

findings.section: L199 / KRN-STATE-01 (L913) vs the new DEFERRED/IGNORED model (L201, KRN-STATE-04)
findings.finding: L199 still says 'every other (state, trigger) pair is invalid: ignored, one invalid-transition entry', and KRN-STATE-01 asserts that every unlisted pair leaves exactly one invalid-transition entry. But (SAVING, any request) is now DEFERRED and later SERVED, and (LOADING, request_shutdown) is DEFERRED. Neither is in the transition table or invalid. A table-driven fixture generated from the tables cannot satisfy both. The 'pair count' note in the registry entry control_plane_request_outcomes (BOOTING rows add 2) is also not reflected anywhere in the GDD text. KRN-STATE-04 asserts DEFERRED and IGNORED, but nothing asserts SERVED, and the diagnostics-surface AC (L1079) does not list the outcome log.
findings.fix: Change L199 and KRN-STATE-01 to: the SAVING pairs are DEFERRED (not invalid), (LOADING, request_shutdown) is DEFERRED, and the other LOADING pairs are IGNORED. Add one fixture row per outcome class, assert SERVED for each tabled transition, and add the outcome log to the L1079 diagnostics-surface list. Request the Debug Overlay counter or reader if it is wanted.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs L798/L799/L804/L815 + constraints 1 and 8 + KRN-BND-01 (carried over)
findings.finding: Several 'safe' ranges break coupled constraints at their own ends. MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK = 32 with the default QUEUE_CAPACITY 1024 gives a drain of 32 ticks, above the 30-tick intent max_age_ticks (constraint 1 fails). QUEUE_CAPACITY = 3840 (the stated ceiling) at MAX_PAYLOAD 4 KiB needs 3840 x 4296 B + 4.1 MiB log, about 19.8 MiB, which exceeds the 16 MiB default budget (constraint 8 fails). MAX_PAYLOAD = 64 KiB fails constraint 8 even at the default queue. COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET = 8 MiB is inside its range, but the defaults need 4.195 + 4.098 = 8.29 MiB, so the range minimum fails the defaults. The table says '8.5 MiB (4.2 + 4.3)' (4.3 is MB, the log is 4.1 MiB) and KRN-BND-01 says 'about 8.5 MiB'.
findings.fix: Restate every range as conditional on constraints 1 and 8 (as QUEUE_CAPACITY already is for constraint 1), or tighten the numeric ranges so each end boots. Set the budget floor at 9 MiB (or the formula) and use one unit (MiB) with the arithmetic 4.195 + 4.098 = 8.29 MiB. Fix the KRN-BND-01 text, and add a boundary AC for MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK = 32.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria L1076 (KRN H1 lint) and CR-14 H1 (carried over)
findings.finding: The member allow-list is {clock, command_queue, registries, binding_tables, command_log, kernel_state, diagnostics} plus {result_buffer, profile, violation_handler}. A faithful implementation also needs the pending control-plane request list and its outcome ledger (CR-15, new this pass), the subscriber list, the seq and submission_id counters (CR-4), host_order, and the runtime knobs (set_knob, constraint 7). The lint fails on a conforming kernel.
findings.fix: Extend the allow-list and the H1 text with pending_requests, request_outcomes, subscribers, counters (seq, submission_id, host_order), knobs, accumulator ownership (the driver, not the kernel), and restore_epoch inside clock.

findings.section: D.12 state_hash fold and canonical_bytes 0x09 PACKED (L603; carried over from reviews 4 and 5)
findings.finding: The fold is written with the glyph '⨁_{b in scope}', which reads as XOR or a sum. It is never stated as ordered byte concatenation, and the widths of len(block_id), schema_version and len(canonical_bytes) are not given. The 0x09 PACKED element-type byte values are not enumerated, and Graph state, the dominant payload, is Packed. state_hash crosses into Save/Load's header as a stored compare value, so two implementations (or a refactor) can hash differently.
findings.fix: Replace the glyph with 'ordered concatenation, ascending block_id bytewise'. State u64 little-endian for each len and u32 for schema_version. Enumerate the element-type bytes (for example 0x01 Byte, 0x02 Int32, 0x03 Int64, 0x04 Float32, 0x05 Float64, 0x06 String, 0x07 Vector2). Add one hand-derived PACKED worked example beside the INT and FLOAT ones.

findings.section: Open Questions 17, 20, 24 (R21)
findings.finding: OQ 17 (CR-9 vs the Debug Overlay's debug-only force_* writes) is still owned by 'user' with resolve-by 'Next consistency pass', although R21 forbids leaving a USER DECISION open. Debug Overlay OQ-DO-11 calls it 'the kernel owner's question', so no GDD holds the decision. OQs 20 and 24 carry no status even though several of their items are done (R14 epoch, BOOTING, the Web Map actor_source declaration) and others are not (see below).
findings.fix: Decide OQ 17 under R21 using the option that needs the least new content and keeps Pillar 1. For example: force_* calls live in a dev-build-only owner debug API, run inside a kernel-issued WriteScope tagged DEV, are logged to the control-plane log, and are compiled out of the release export (KRN-SEAM-01 symbol scan). Mark OQ 17 resolved by delegated ruling R21. Split OQ 20 and 24 into per-item DONE / OPEN lines.

findings.section: Cross-GDD stale references (OQ 20 / OQ 24 items still open; this pass touched Pixel-Perfect and left it stale)
findings.finding: The kernel contract (CR-1a: input is sampled in the driver's _process, the physics callback is not the tick source) conflicts with these sibling texts. player-controller-input.md L1021 says 'Input is sampled in the physics callback' and AC-PCI-003 (L1077) expects the sample in 'the same physics callback' as Kernel.step(), which would fail against a conforming driver. suit-and-equipment.md L1441 repeats the physics-callback wording. pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md L227, L297 and L1219 (the file was edited this pass) still say 'kernel D.4 assumes the physics callback drives the tick' and ask for physics_ticks_per_second and max_physics_steps_per_frame to be matched. attention-system.md AT-8 (L196) and L579 write rng_derive(world_seed, 'attention.tell', counter_eff) inline instead of calling rng_derive_epoch, so the RNG_COUNTER_RANGE_VIOLATION guard is bypassed (Horror was fixed this pass).
findings.fix: Route the edits to each file's writer. Player Controller: rewrite L1021 and AC-PCI-003 to adapter -> driver -> presentation order (KRN-LAT-02). Suit: reword L1441. Pixel-Perfect: replace L227/L297/L1219 with CR-1a and close its OQ 10. Attention: call rng_derive_epoch(world_seed, 'attention.tell', rng_counter). Keep OQ 20/24 open until a grep for 'physics callback' in these files is clean.

findings.section: Dependencies / systems-index.md / Header
findings.finding: The seven presentation-consumer 'No - add edge' rows (Pixel-Perfect, Lighting, Failure & Trail, HUD, Instruments, Audio, Chart Table) are still missing from systems-index.md. The Co-op row (L775) is not labelled undesigned / provisional contract (R9). The CD-GDD-ALIGN approval (2026-10-25) has not been re-run after four amendment rounds.
findings.fix: Add the seven kernel edges to the index. Relabel the Co-op row 'undesigned - provisional contract: MIRROR mode, ingress adapter, binding-table API'. Run a CD alignment spot-check at the next review, or record a delegated waiver.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria L1074, KRN-EPO-05 (L989), L1101
findings.finding: Three ACs are untestable as written. (1) L1074 'the reviewer ticks a verb cost <= 2 files checkbox' is a human checkbox with no mechanical test. (2) KRN-EPO-05 asserts 'no frame between DEAD and LOADING blocked the main thread for longer than one poll', and 'one poll' has no duration. (3) L1101 'kernel overhead ... is recorded' has no pass line (intentional until the spike).
findings.fix: (1) Rewrite as a lint/diff test: 'a fixture PR adding one command type touches <= 2 files under src/, counted by git diff --name-only; a 3rd file fails the CI check'. (2) Quote: 'longest main-thread frame time between the DEAD transition and LOADING <= FRAME_SIM_BUDGET_MS(1) (4.0 ms), measured with the staged write held for 600 ms'. (3) Add 'pass line frozen by the spike; until then the AC is evidence-only and tagged (spike)'.

findings.finding: The golden-vector note says 'the horror.tell / rng_int(600, 1800) usage matches Horror's HE-9 stream use'. That range belongs to attention.tell, and Horror derives its unfold with UNFOLD_LO/HI. The D.6 frame example still uses P3 = 2.9 ms, above the kernel's own 2.0 ms P3 P99 target. FRAME_SIM_BUDGET_MS(4) computes to 6.001 from the stated formula, while the AC and table say 6.0.
findings.fix: State that the vectors are stream-name examples and that the stream-use claim lives with Attention and Horror. Use P3 <= 2.0 ms in the D.6 example. Use ceil-to-0.1 or '4.0 + (n-1) x 2/3 = 6.0' so the formula and the 6.0 gate agree.

findings.section: States L166 (BOOTING cell) and Open Question 15
findings.finding: The BOOTING cell cites 'Chart Table TX-30, EC-CT-37' for 'the main menu and boot-flow screens run with the kernel in this state'. Those rows only specify the Quit path (request_shutdown from BOOTING). The menu-in-BOOTING claim is the kernel's own, and OQ 15 still records the composition-root order as open. A first-boot new game also takes default_state() for PROFILE-scoped blocks without saying how Save/Load's profile image is applied (zero PROFILE blocks at MVP, so no MVP impact).
findings.fix: Reword the BOOTING citation to 'Quit from the menu: TX-30, EC-CT-37' and keep the idle-until-first-request rule as the kernel's. Add one sentence to the BOOTING + request_new_game row that a PROFILE image, when blocks exist, is applied by Save/Load through the cold-open restore path before the new game (VS).

data.summary: Verdict: APPROVED, confirming the 2026-10-28 approval. There are no BLOCKING items. The three recommended blockers from the prior review are RESOLVED in the kernel GDD, and I re-verified the Web Map and Save/Load sibling edits. The BOOTING first-boot rows, the DEFERRED/IGNORED model and the SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE spelling hold together, and the new ACs (KRN-STATE-03/04) are mechanical. The receipt check shows both files CHANGED, as expected after this pass. The structure check shows all 8 sections PRESENT, and 25 of 26 dependency GDDs exist; only the undesigned VS-B Co-op GDD is missing, which R9 allows. Numbers are consistent with the registry: the D.5 accumulator examples, the 8-tick drain, the latency percentiles, the lcm-60 worst tick, and the 4.195 + 4.098 MiB memory arithmetic at the defaults. Most of the 12 recommended findings are carried over from the last two reviews (the driver loop with atomic restore, the tuning-range vs constraint 1 and 8 breaks, the incomplete H1 allow-list, the unspecified D.12 fold and PACKED bytes, OQ 17 still user-owned, stale physics-callback text in sibling GDDs). Two are new from this pass: a boot-time registry FAULTED is not terminal, so request_new_game can load past an invalid registry, and the new DEFERRED/IGNORED outcomes contradict the old 'every other pair is invalid' rule and KRN-STATE-01. No 'Resolved ... user ruling' or 'delegated ruling Rn' marker is reversed or contradicted.
